short: An iconic, highly maneuverable British fighter credited with destroying more enemy aircraft than any other Allied type.
full:
Introduced in June 1917, the Sopwith Camel was a legendary British biplane fighter characterised by its immense maneuverability and demanding handling characteristics. Its powerful rotary engine created severe torque effects, making the aircraft notoriously difficult for novice pilots to master and leading to many fatal training accidents. However, in the hands of an experienced aviator, this instability allowed for phenomenally quick turns that no contemporary enemy fighter could match.

The Camel became the primary weapon of the Royal Naval Air Service and the Royal Flying Corps during the latter half of the war. Armed with twin synchronized Vickers machine guns, it was brutally effective in combat and is credited with downing nearly 1,300 enemy aircraft, the highest total of any single Allied design. Despite its stellar combat record, its difficult handling led to rapid postwar obsolescence, and it was withdrawn from Royal Air Force service in January 1920.
